articles.title: KV Cache VRAM Calculator: How Much Memory Does Context Length Need? (2026)
articles.excerpt: The KV cache is the memory a transformer uses to remember every token in the context, and its size grows linearly with context length: bytes per token = 2 × layers × KV heads × head dimension × bytes…
articles.body: The KV cache is the memory a transformer uses to remember every token in the context, and its size grows linearly with context length: bytes per token = 2 × layers × KV heads × head dimension × bytes per value. For Qwen3 32B at FP16 that is 256 KiB per token, or about 8 GB for a 32k-token context, on top of the model weights. This is why a model that loads fine can still run out of memory when you raise the context. This post gives the formula, the per-token numbers for popular open models (read from their config.json ), and how much context fits on 24, 32, 48 and 80 GB cards. The formula kv_bytes_per_token = 2 × num_hidden_layers × num_key_value_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value kv_total_bytes = kv_bytes_per_token × context_tokens × concurrent_sequences The 2 is for keys and values.

articles.title: JavaScript number precision for large IDs, and ten new features for agent code
articles.excerpt: A long numeric ID can come out of JSON.parse as a different number, and nothing throws. const text = '{"id":1234567890123456789}' const { id } = JSON.parse(text) BigInt(id) // 1234567890123456768n JSO…
articles.body: A long numeric ID can come out of JSON.parse as a different number, and nothing throws. const text = ' {"id":1234567890123456789} ' const { id } = JSON . parse ( text ) BigInt ( id ) // 1234567890123456768n JSON . stringify ({ id }) // '{"id":1234567890123456800}' JavaScript numbers are 64-bit floats. Every whole number up to 9,007,199,254,740,991 ( Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER ) is exact. Above that, only some whole numbers fit, and among 19-digit numbers they're 128 to 2,048 apart. JSON.parse rounds the ID to the nearest one that fits ( MDN , ECMA-262 ). So the ID changes twice. Parsing rounds it, which BigInt(id) shows: the original digits are gone, and no conversion brings them back.

articles.title: ☁️ OneDrive Stuck on "Sync Pending"? Fix It Before You Reinstall
articles.excerpt: A user calls: "My files aren't syncing." The spinning arrows have been spinning since Tuesday. 😩 The temptation is to uninstall OneDrive and start fresh. Don't. Most sync problems come down to three…
articles.body: A user calls: "My files aren't syncing." The spinning arrows have been spinning since Tuesday. 😩 The temptation is to uninstall OneDrive and start fresh. Don't. Most sync problems come down to three things: the client is paused or signed out, one problem file is blocking the queue, or the local sync state is confused. Here's the order I check them in. 🔍 1. Read the status first Click the OneDrive cloud icon in the taskbar notification area (you may need the ^ arrow to find it). Look for: Paused : someone paused sync (or it auto-paused on battery saver / metered network). Click Resume . Signed out / grey cloud : the account isn't signed in. Sign back in. Red X or "sync issues" : click it. OneDrive usually lists the exact file it's stuck on. Storage full : the OneDrive quota is used up.

articles.excerpt: The fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was one giant gimmick: shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres.
articles.body: It didn’t take long for fans to figure out that the fourth season of "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" was going to be unlike any season of " Star Trek " before it. The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react. It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. That should trouble any Trekkie.

articles.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (photos)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX sent 27 more of its Starlink broadband satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23), in its first Starlink launch in 11 days.
articles.body: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p.m. local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes. The Falcon 9's first stage, shortly after its drone-ship landing on Oct. 23, 2026.
